background_notes.fact: For a jointly smooth map u on R^n×(0,∞), e=|u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² is smooth and its time derivative is 2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, a continuous real function on that open domain.

grounds.reason: Joint C∞ regularity supplies continuous derivatives of every needed order on the open domain.
The derivatives and Euclidean scalar product have their componentwise classical meanings.
e is exactly the finite sum of squared norms, with no normalization factor.

background_notes.justification: Write each squared norm as the finite sum of squares of real components and apply the scalar product rule. For each component, continuous second partial derivatives allow ∂t∂x_j u=∂x_j∂t u. Finite sums and products of the resulting continuous derivatives are continuous. Smoothness also gives continuity of e and its spatial slices used subsequently.

background_notes.justification: Closed bounded boxes in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces are compact; their product with a closed bounded real interval is another such box. Its positive-time inclusion permits restriction of the continuous function |e_t|. The continuous image of this compact set is compact in R and therefore bounded; since the function is nonnegative one can choose a finite B≥0. This is the local compactness/maximum argument already invoked in S003.
